target_name: Cash Yield x Organic-minus-Acquired Intangible Mix
rationale: The signed organic-minus-acquired composition score is a genuine structural fix to the gen-0 winner's degenerate zero-goodwill tie block rather than a cosmetic re-parameterization, and switching the value leg to pre-R&D operating cash flow is an economically motivated (not merely mechanical) attempt to convert a strong cross-sectional slope into a reliable portfolio alpha, though it remains close enough to the archived winner that a null result would be uninformative.

This is the archived "Demeaned Value x Off-Balance-Sheet Capital Share" with the R&D scaler swapped from an asset-stock to sales and, more seriously, with the expected sign reversed post hoc to match the previously observed negative estimate — that is sign-fitting to a known result rather than a new hypothesis, and BM interacted with R&D-to-sales is itself a long-published interaction (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis).

target_name: Intangible Profit Yield vs Implied Intangible Price
rationale: The stated mechanism is internally inconsistent — because the two legs are separately rank-transformed, the "identical denominator" never cancels and cannot produce a price-versus-payoff spread, leaving what is operationally a conventional industry-neutral gross-profitability-minus-valuation composite (Novy-Marx plus value) whose second leg is also ill-behaved when market value falls below book equity.

The core hypothesis — high-valuation firms making goodwill-generating acquisitions subsequently underperform — is the published glamour-acquirer/asset-growth anomaly (Rau-Vermaelen; Cooper-Gulen-Schill), and the ZSCORE product additionally lumps cheap firms taking goodwill *impairments* into the same extreme tail as expensive serial acquirers, so the signal's short leg conflates two economically distinct populations.

target_name: Scale-Free Intangible Productivity Trend vs Sales Price
rationale: The diagnosis of the gen-0 failure is specific and correct (raw TREND scales with the series level, and the `intan` denominator both truncated coverage to 8% and created near-zero-denominator artifacts), and normalizing the slope by its own five-year mean plus re-basing on total assets plus the R&D stock is a real fix — but the mean-normalized trend can still blow up for firms with low average intangible productivity, and the sales-to-price value leg is unchanged, so the alpha problem may well persist.

This is a near-duplicate of the archived "Cheapness x Intangible-Inclusive Gross Profitability" — the same industry-relative intangible-inclusive gross profitability conditioner on a value leg, differing only by ZSCORE-versus-RANK and BM-versus-EBITDA/P — which is precisely the cosmetic variant of an already-failed signal (ls_talpha −0.55) that the objective warns against.
